clues.narrowing: One old river city in the north of France, built on an island in its river.

source.quote: Paris is located in northern central France, in a north-bending arc of the river Seine, whose crest includes two islands, the Île Saint-Louis and the larger Île de la Cité, which form the oldest part of Paris.

clues.text: This city grew around a small island in a wide, winding river that flows west to the sea. A steep hill rises to its north.

clues.narrowing: The weather points to the west side of Europe: mild, grey, and rainy all year.

source.quote: Paris has an average annual precipitation of 641 mm (25.2 in), and experiences light rainfall distributed evenly throughout the year.

clues.text: Winters here are cool and grey, and soft rain can fall in any month of the year. Summers are warm but seldom hot, and the sky is often grey.

clues.narrowing: An old trading town that later gained a famous church with two towers.

source.quote: Maurice de Sully, bishop of Paris, started the construction of the Notre Dame Cathedral in 1163, and was completed after 182 years.

clues.text: Traders came by river and settled that island more than 2,000 years ago. Much later, a great stone church with two tall towers was begun on the same island.

clues.narrowing: One famous iron tower points at this city.

source.quote: Originally commissioned as a temporary structure for the 1889 Exposition Universelle, Eiffel was slated for dismantling in 1909, at which point ownership would have reverted to the City of Paris.

clues.text: A lacy iron tower rose for a fair in 1889, built to be torn down when the fair's years ran out. People loved it so much it stayed, and now it is the sign of the city.

clues.narrowing: Only a capital has the president's palace and the lawmakers.

source.quote: The President of the French Republic resides at the Élysée Palace.

clues.text: The president of France lives and works in a palace in this city, and the laws of the land are made here too. This city is the capital of France.

reveal.blurb: Paris began as an island village in the River Seine more than 2,000 years ago. It grew into France's capital, where kings, artists, and inventors shaped its streets. Today that iron tower from 1889 still watches over it. Spot it, and remember: Paris is the capital of France.
